messages.text: 'A huge milestone' - Kartal becomes second Brit ever to reach WTA 1000 final

metadata.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal was forced to dig deep to beat Jelena Ostapenko and secure a spot in her first-ever WTA 1000 final on Saturday.
metadata.content: Sonay Kartal: British star digs deep to beat Jelena Ostapenko and secure a spot in her first-ever WTA 1000 final | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sonay Kartal: British star digs deep to beat Jelena Ostapenko and secure a spot in her first-ever WTA 1000 final Sonay Kartal defeats Jelena Ostapenko to reach her first-ever WTA 1000 final against former world No 1 Iga Swiatek or French Open finalist Maja Chwalinska; You can watch the WTA Wuhan Open final - live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 11.30am Raz Mirza Sports Journalist @RazMirza Saturday 17 October 2026 14:13, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open semi-final between Sonay Kartal and Jelena Ostapenko Britain's Sonay Kartal was forced to dig deep to beat Jelena Ostapenko and secure a spot in her first-ever WTA 1000 final on Saturday. Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Ostapenko. Currently 170th in the WTA rankings, Kartal will break inside the top 50 and become the new British No 1 after becoming the lowest-ranked player to reach the final in Wuhan. The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match. messages.text: Red Roses' 41-game unbeaten run ended in dramatic fashion

metadata.summary: England's 41-game unbeaten run is over after they were stunned by a late rally from Canada, the Red Roses falling 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto.
metadata.content: WXV Global Series: England stunned by a late rally from Canada as Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run ends with 24-21 loss | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WXV Global Series: England stunned by a late rally from Canada as Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run ends with 24-21 loss Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday Saturday 17 October 2026 07:53, UK Image: Canada ended England's 41-game unbeaten run England's 41-game unbeaten run is over after they were stunned by a late rally from Canada, the Red Roses falling 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto. Shoshanah Seumanutafa came off the bench to score the match-winning try in the 77th minute to hand England their first defeat since the 2022 World Cup final. Following a draw in their previous clash last month in Exeter , Canada looked up for the challenge early as they opened the scoring through Savannah Bauder in the 15th minute. messages.text: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux

metadata.summary: Will Trenholm’s brace was not enough to help Gloucester pull off a stunning upset against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux, as they were forced to settle for a 36-36 draw after a dramatic contest.
metadata.content: Champions Cup: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against holders Bordeaux | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Champions Cup: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against holders Bordeaux Will Trenholm scores a brace of tries as Gloucester fall just short of beating Champions Cup holders Bordeaux in a thrilling 36-36 draw; Edinburgh suffered a 27-17 defeat against Toulon in their Challenge Cup opener Friday 16 October 2026 22:53, UK Image: Will Trenholm celebrates as Gloucester draws with Bordeaux in the Investec Champions Cup Will Trenholm’s brace was not enough to help Gloucester pull off a stunning upset against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux, as they were forced to settle for a 36-36 draw after a dramatic contest. George Skivington's team pushed the French outfit all the way during a pulsating European tie at Kingsholm Stadium. Gloucester held a 24-17 lead at half-time before Trenholm crashed over twice, but a double by Louis Bielle-Biarrey salvaged a share of the spoils for visiting Bordeaux.
